==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/fɪt/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-fit.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪt|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=suitable|:inh|enm:fit<t:an adversary of equal power><unc>|tree=1}}
Possibly from {{inh|en|enm|fit||an adversary of equal power}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} further origin. The original sense appears to have been "to marshal or deploy troops", which shifted to "to suit (troops to a certain location" > "suitable", and may be further related to {{cog|is|fitja|t=to web, knit, cast on}}.<ref>https://www.etymonline.com/word/fit#etymonline_v_5980</ref>

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|er}}

# {{cap|suitable}}; [[proper]]
#: {{ux|en|You have nothing to say about it. I'll do exactly as I see '''fit'''.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Job|34|18|passage=Is it '''fit''' to say a king, Thou art wicked?}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1902|author=John Buchan|title=The Outgoing of the Tide
|passage=He had drunk more than was '''fit''' for him, and he was singing some light song, when he saw approaching, as he said, the pale horse mentioned in the Revelation, with Death seated as the rider.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|by=w:Plato|title=Sophist|author=Lesley Brown|note=[[w:Stephanus pagination|243d]]
|passage=The rest we'll leave to be examined later, if we think '''fit''';}}
# [[adapt|Adapted]] to a [[purpose]] or [[environment]].
#: {{ux|en|survival of the '''fittest'''}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear|I|iv|passage=That which ordinary men are '''fit''' for, I am qualified in.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Ariane de Vogue|title=Why Clarence Thomas wrote over a dozen pages on eugenics|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/05/28/politics/clarence-thomas-eugenics-abortion|date=2019-05-28|passage=Wading through history, he noted that some eugenicists believed that the “distinction between the '''fit''' and the unfit could be drawn along racial lines,” and others would define a person as “feeble-minded.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250820204953/https://www.cnn.com/2019/05/28/politics/clarence-thomas-eugenics-abortion|archivedate=20 August 2025}}
# In [[good]] [[shape]]; [[physically]] [[well]].
#: {{ux|en|You don't have to be a good climber for Kilimanjaro, but you do have to be '''fit'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:Men's Health|year=2026|issue=2|volume=41|title=The Most Important Health Metric You're Not Tracking|author=Ginny Graves|page=19
|text=Even the '''fittest''' among us may have problems, because hypertension can be genetic or stem from kidney problems or sleep apnea, and the risk typically increases with age.}}
# {{lb|en|British|informal|chiefly|slang}} {{cap|sexually}} [[attractive]]; [[good-looking]]; [[fanciable]].
#: {{ux|en|I think the girl working in the office is '''fit'''.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|author={{w|Mike Skinner (musician)|Mike Skinner}}|title=w:Fit but You Know It|album=A Grand Don't Come for Free|artist=The Streets|year=2004|passage=I think you are really '''fit''' / You're '''fit''' but my gosh don't you know it.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|lyricist=Kate Nash; Paul Eppworth|title={{w|Foundations (song)|Foundations}}|album=Made of Bricks|artist=Kate Nash|year=2007|passage=I said I'd rather be with your friends, mate, cos they are much '''fitter'''.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} {{cap|prepared}}; [[ready]].
#* {{RQ:Tasso Fairfax Godfrey of Bulloigne
|passage=So '''fit''' to shoot, she singled forth among her foes who first her quarry's strength should feel.}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb|+|+|+,~}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be [[suitable]] for.
#: {{ux|en|It '''fits''' the purpose.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To have sufficient [[space]] available at some location to be able to be there.
#: {{ux|en|Ten clowns '''fit''' in the car, but not a hundred.}}
#: {{ux|en|The elevator can '''fit''' up to 10 people.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To conform to in [[size]] and [[shape]].
#: {{ux|en|The small shirt doesn't '''fit''' me, so I'll buy the medium size.}}
#: {{ux|en|If I lose a few kilos, the gorgeous wedding dress might '''fit''' me.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be of the right [[size]] and [[shape]]
#: {{syn|en|sit}}
#* {{quote-song|en|year=1947|artist=w:Hank Williams|title={{w|Move It On Over (song)|Move It On Over}}|text=She's changed the lock on our front door / My door key don't fit no more}}
#* {{quote-song|en|lyricist={{w|Maynard James Keenan}}|composer={{w|Adam Jones (musician)|Adam Jones}}, {{w|Danny Carey}}, Maynard James Keenan, and {{w|Justin Chancellor}}|title={{w|Schism (song)|Schism}}|album={{w|Lateralus}}|artist={{w|Tool (band)|Tool}}|year=2001|note=track 5|text=I know the pieces '''fit''' / 'Cause I watched them fall away}}
#* {{quote-av|en|date=February 2 2016|author=w:Kate Winslet; et al|url=https://vine.co/v/iJAlIziXMKv|title=Jimmy Kimmel Live!
|passage=Even though in a way you let him freeze to death in the water, because the way I see it... / I agree. [[y'know|Y'know]], I think he actually could have '''fitted''' on that bit of door. / There was plenty of room on the raft. / I know. I know, I know.}}
#: {{ux|en|I wanted to borrow my little sister's jeans, but they didn't '''fit'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|That plug '''fitted''' into the other socket, but it won't go in this one.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|with ''to''}} To make conform in size and shape.
#: {{nearsyn|en|fit up<qq:often synonymous>}}
#: {{ux|en|I want to '''fit''' the drapes to the windows.}}
#: {{ux|en|The [[fitter]]s will '''fit''' the tooling so that the production line can then [[crank up]].}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[tailor]]; to change to the appropriate size.
##: {{ux|en|I had a suit '''fitted''' by the tailor.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be in agreement with.
#: {{ux|en|These definitions '''fit''' most of the usage.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|page=427|chapter=Old English maþelian, mæþlan, mǣlan|author=Don Ringe|title=Indo-European Perspectives: Studies in Honour of Anna Morpurgo Davies|editor=J. H. W. Penney|publisher=w:Oxford University Press|isbn=9780199258925|date=14 October 2004|url=https://books.google.co.nz/books/?id=T1YTDAAAQBAJ|text=Type D half-lines ending in words of this type are analysed by Hutcheson as ending in two completely unstressed syllables. That analysis must be descriptively correct for, say, the 10th cent.; whether it would have '''fitted''' the facts in the 8th cent. is much less clear.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[adjust]].
#: {{ux|en|The regression program '''fit''' a line to the data.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[attach]], especially when requiring exact positioning or sizing.
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[equip]] or [[supply]].
#: {{nearsyn|en|fit out<qq:often synonymous>}}
#: {{ux|en|The [[chandler]] will '''fit''' us with [[provision]]s for a month.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make ready.
#: {{syn|en|fix to<q:US, informal>}}
#: {{ux|en|I’m '''fitting''' the ship for a summer sail home.}}
#: {{ux|en|I’m '''fitting''' to go home and sleep.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1846|quotee=w:Emily Dickinson|title=letter|quoted_in=''Lives Like Loaded Guns: Emily Dickinson and Her Family's Feuds''|author=Lyndall Gordon|year_published=2010|passage='I am '''fitting''' to go to South Hadley Seminary [as Mount Holyoke was known], and expect if my health is good to enter that institution a year from next fall', she confided to Abiah.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|archaic}} To be [[seemly]].
# To be proper or becoming.
#* {{RQ:Homer Pope et al Odyssey|book=III|passage=Nor '''fits''' it to prolong the heav'nly feast.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be in harmony.
#: {{syn|en|mesh}}
#: {{ux|en|The paint, the fabrics, the rugs all '''fit'''.}}

=====Usage notes=====
* In senses 1 to 6, this is generally a [[stative verb]] that rarely takes the continuous inflection. See [[:Category:English stative verbs]]

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# The degree to which something fits.
#: {{ux|en|This shirt is a bad '''fit'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|Since he put on weight, his jeans have been a tight '''fit'''.}}
# Conformity of elements one to another.
#: {{ux|en|It's hard to get a good '''fit''' using second-hand parts.}}
# The part of an object upon which anything fits tightly.
# {{lb|en|advertising}} Measure of how well a particular commercial execution captures the character or values of a brand.
#: {{ux|en|The Wonder Bread advertising research results showed the “White Picket Fence” commercial had strong '''fit''' ratings.}}
# {{lb|en|statistics}} Goodness of fit.
# {{lb|en|bridge}} The quality of a partnership's combined holding of cards in a [[suit]], particularly of [[trump]].
#: {{ux|en|During the auction, it is often a partnership's goal to find an eight-card major suit '''fit'''.}}

===Etymology 2===
{{ety|en|id=section|:inh<unc>|ang:fitt<t:song>}}
{{unk|en}}, possibly from {{inh|en|ang|fitt||song}}, or from the sense of ''fitted'' to length. Compare {{cog|osx|*fittea}} (attested in the borrowed {{cog|la|vittea}}).

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|archaic}} A [[section]] of a [[poem]] or [[ballad]].

====References====
* Oxford English Dictionary: fit, fyte n. 1

===Etymology 3===
{{ety|en|id=sudden activity}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeygʷ-}}<!--but unlikely; missing Cornish etymon's root-->
{{unk|en}}. From {{inh|en|enm|fit||hardship, danger}}, possibly from {{inh|en|ang|fitt||conflict}}—a word only attested once.<ref>{{R:OED Online|fit|n|1150155610}}</ref> Compare {{cog|kw|fit||game match, bout}}; or else, maybe cognate with {{cog|it|fitta||sudden and stabbing pain}} (see further at {{der|en|la|figo|fīgere}}).

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|seizure or convulsion}} A [[seizure]] or [[convulsion]].
#: {{ux|en|My grandfather died after having a '''fit'''.}}
# {{lb|en|medicine}} A [[sudden]] and [[vigorous]] [[appearance]] of a [[symptom]] over a short period of time.
# {{senseid|en|sudden outburst of emotion}} A [[sudden]] [[outburst]] of [[emotion]].
#: {{syn|en|spell#Noun|moment}}
#: {{hypo|en|blowout|tantrum|hissy#Noun|hissy fit|shit fit|snit#Noun|snit fit|duck fit}}
#: {{ux|en|He had a laughing '''fit''' which lasted more than ten minutes.}}
#: {{ux|en|She had a '''fit''' and threw all of his clothes out through the window.}}
#: {{ux|en|He threw a '''fit''' (of [[temper]]) when his car broke down.}}
# A sudden [[burst]] (of an activity).
#: {{syn|en|flurry|frenzy|paroxysm}}
